what: The public change log of /r310/: one dated entry per change of the page or of its state. The builder refuses when the newest entry’s state is not the records’.

entries.what: First build of the page, unpublished, for the control room's review: the case map (12 cases), box 1 (Theorem C35) and box 2 (the second computation of Case R(7)) opened, box 3 sealed with its three Bitcoin anchors and its progress, the replay of the R(7) run, the corrections ledger and the machine at work.

The page follows the reveal's source of truth (REVEAL-v2, 23 Nov): its title is now “R(3,10), in the open”; box 2 says first that Chen’s run closed the case, with C-004’s round 1 and its round-2 confirmation, and prints the correction of a sentence of its sealed text; box 1 cites the two other places the C35 question was posed and the prose corollary; the credits name each model; two errors added to the ledger.

Revisions from the control room before the first look: the sealed box at its newest ledger copy (05:38 UTC); the corrections ledger shows five that mattered and its timeline, with all 55 rows and their sources one click down; the opening time of boxes 1 and 2 is set at publication; Kalbfleisch credited for the circulant, as Goedgebeur and Radziszowski credit him; the S8 case marked as resting on unpublished enumeration runs.
Boxes 1 and 2 opened at publication: Theorem C35 and the second computation of R(7), with the record of both seals at corpus/r310-c35-r7/.

A phase finished: box 1 now says why the bound is 39, shows Exoo’s square (the theorem’s equality case in Exoo’s 1989 graph) and a smaller certificate for Lemma P (385 sets in five orbits), both found in a reading by GPT-6.2-astra and checked by our own code; box 2 links the full R(7) ledger, now published as a sealed reveal, and reports that its two full-formula configurations were regenerated byte for byte on a laptop; five checks added to the machine’s tally.

Credits corrected: Unsolved Lab already reported that Exoo's graph is C35 plus four vertices in exactly one way; the deletion corollary was derived in a GPT-6.2-astra reading. The programs behind Exoo's square and the 385-set certificate are added to the record (c35/review-check/).

A phase finished: the sealed box at its newest ledger copy; a second machine for it ran and is deleted; one discrepancy inside the sealed box is open and under investigation, and until it is decided no input it touches counts as closed.

A phase finished: the discrepancy inside the sealed box is resolved. The second program was the one in error and ours was right; every input it touched was decided anyway, and no verdict changes. The sealed box has no open discrepancy.
The sealed box reaches 100%: the sealed computation has a result for every one of its inputs. It stays sealed; it opens only after its audit, on Carlos Toledo's word.
